19.notes: Hint 1 does not just orient attention, it already states the defining trait of the correct option. It reads: 'The accusers were a group of the king's own wise men and officials in Babylon.' In Daniel, 'Chaldeans' is precisely the term used for the king's wise men and astrologers, so a student who knows that pairs the description straight to option C without needing hints 2 or 3. That is the decisive principle hint 2 is supposed to supply, and hint 2 nearly repeats it anyway ('The accusers came from Babylon's own people'), which makes hints 1 and 2 redundant and pitches hint 1 too strong. Applying the standard's own test for hint 1, 'if it would help a student on a different question in the same topic, it is pitched right': knowing the accusers were the king's wise men and officials would not help on another faith.furnace question (e.g. who threw them in the furnace, or what the fourth man in the fire meant), so it is specific to this answer rather than a generic orientation.
19.fix: Recall Daniel 3:8, and notice which group at Nebuchadnezzar's court is named as the ones who came forward and made the accusation.
